acceptance_criteria.how_to_check: py -3.11 scripts/drive/d1016_f663_calls_dir_clean.py <name> (written first: fails before the build)

acceptance_criteria.then: the directory is empty and the link's target still holds its file

acceptance_criteria.then: the file is still there; an agent with its own worktree finds its directory empty

design: Tier 1, no migration. D1: prepare_calls_dir(work_dir, *, empty) with no default; the call site passes isolated_workspace is not None. Emptying runs after the existing link handling: an entry that is a link or junction (normcase(realpath) differs) is removed as a link (rmdir on nt for a directory link, else unlink), a file is unlinked, a real subdirectory is rmtree'd. A shared workspace (project directory, explicit work_dir) is never emptied: another agent's file may be in flight there. D2: one sentence in launchability.access_path_notice and agents._tool_surface_lines' shim preamble asks for a new file name per call and a new file for corrected arguments. D3: each removal is best effort (OSError logged as a warning, the turn proceeds); failing to make the directory is still refused 409. D4: Copilot's spec-turn exclusions stay (create is kept). This reverses D14 of a-run-reaches-the-hub-without-mcp ('the agent may reuse them').

checked: prepare_calls_dir ends with makedirs(exist_ok=True) and removes no file
home drive on a scratch Hub (f663before2): Haiku Write refused the previous turn's create_task.json ('File has not been read yet')
limits: No Copilot turn at home; Copilot's create refusal is the work-PC record

problem: prepare_calls_dir makes the calls directory but never removes a file, and both shim texts give the example name 1.json. A new conversation cannot know a file is already there; Copilot's create and Claude Haiku 4.5's Write refuse to overwrite an unread file. Work PC: the second shim turn's create failed twice and cost 151k tokens instead of ~75k (F663); the Copilot spec turn's failed write (F664) was the same leftover, since create is kept on spec turns. Reproduced at home on a scratch Hub: a Haiku shim turn in a new conversation chose the previous turn's create_task.json, Write answered 'File has not been read yet', and the turn fell back to Set-Content.

requirements.rationale: A new conversation cannot know an earlier file exists, and write tools refuse to overwrite an unread file.
requirements.statement: When a turn's workspace is isolated (the agent's own worktree, a task checkout or a review checkout), its .agentweave/calls/ directory MUST hold no entry from an earlier turn when the run starts; a link or junction inside it MUST be removed as a link without touching its target.

requirements.rationale: Another agent's arguments file may be in flight there.
requirements.statement: A calls directory in a workspace that is not isolated (the project directory, an explicit work_dir) MUST NOT be emptied at turn start.

requirements.rationale: A leftover costs a retry; a blocked agent costs the turn.
requirements.statement: An entry that cannot be removed MUST be logged as a warning and the turn MUST start; failing to make the directory itself MUST still refuse the turn as before.

requirements.rationale: Covers a name reused within one turn and any shared workspace.
requirements.statement: Both texts that tell a run the call command (the turn-start notice and the tool-surface preamble) MUST ask it to use a new file name for each call and to write corrected arguments to a new file rather than editing an old one.

in_scope: prepare_calls_dir empties the directory in an isolated workspace, links removed as links
the trigger passes empty for isolated workspaces only
both call-mode texts ask for a new file name per call
an emptying failure warns and the turn proceeds
non_goals: The shared project-directory race between two read-only agents (wpc4-c)
A per-agent or per-run calls subdirectory
Giving Copilot spec turns a replace tool (wpc5-a: edit stays excluded)

summary: At turn start the Hub empties .agentweave/calls/ when the turn's workspace is isolated (the agent's own worktree, a task checkout, a review checkout), and both call-mode texts ask for a new arguments file name per call, so a new conversation no longer collides with an earlier turn's file (F663, F664; decision fix-D6 / wpc4-a (a2)). Re-authored from openspec a-call-file-turn-starts-clean-and-can-write-its-file.
